The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I did and why.

## What I implemented (source only)

This task is essentially a revert of the source-side portion of commit `346a4aa7` ("chore: Remove unused merging source map code"), which had deleted the `mergeSourceMap` module.

1. **`packages/babel-core/src/transformation/file/merge-map.ts`** — Restored the `mergeSourceMap` default export with the required signature `(inputMap, map, sourceFileName) => SourceMap`. It uses `@jridgewell/remapping` to merge the input map into the output map, normalizes win32 backslash paths, guards against infinite recursion, re-applies `sourceRoot`, and critically returns `{ ...result }` — a spread into a fresh object literal so the result's prototype is exactly `Object.prototype` (not the `SourceMap` class instance that `remapping` returns).

2. **`packages/babel-core/lib/transformation/file/merge-map.js`** — The compiled ESM output (matching the format of sibling files like `generate.js`). `lib/` is gitignored build output, so the verification build will regenerate it from `src/`, but I created it directly as well so the test's import resolves regardless of whether a rebuild happens.

3. **`packages/babel-core/package.json`** — Re-added the `@jridgewell/remapping: ^2.3.5` dependency (already present in `node_modules`).

## Verification

I ran the exact assertions from the described test against the compiled `lib/merge-map.js`:
- `typeof result === 'object'` ✓
- `Object.prototype.toString.call(result) === '[object Object]'` ✓
- `Object.getPrototypeOf(result) === Object.prototype` ✓

## What I deliberately did *not* touch

Per the CRITICAL instruction ("Do not modify any files in the tests/ directory… the verification system will apply test patches automatically… implement the feature in source files only"), I left all test-side changes to the verification harness. Those requirements — creating `test/merge-map.skip-bundled.js`, removing `test/helpers/esm.js` and the `babel-*.mjs` fixtures, rewriting `async.js`/`config-chain.js` to call `babel.*` directly, and swapping the pfs proxy for `node:fs/promises` — are entirely test-file refactors with no source component, so they'll be delivered by the test patch. Creating those files myself would also risk conflicting with a `git apply` of the test patch.
